raw_response:
I am here in Mangochi with my 0.78 hectare maize plot, and I must think carefully. Last season I got some FISP coupon and it helped me buy one bag of NPK and one bag of urea — I hope I get the coupon again this year, because without it the fertilizer price at the agro-dealer in town is too much for me. I plant hybrid seed when I can get it through the coupon, and I mix in some groundnut and pumpkin between my maize rows like my father did. I have no irrigation here — my plot depends on the rains from November, and I weed with my wife and our two older children, though at planting and first weeding I sometimes pay a neighbor's son a few days to help me finish before the weeds take over.

For fertilizer, I will apply what I can — about one bag of NPK 23-21-0 at planting and one bag of urea at knee-high, spread across my maize rows. That is roughly 100 kg of urea and 100 kg of NPK on my 0.78 ha, so maybe around 70 kg of nitrogen per hectare if I stretch it properly. I also carry some manure from my few goats to the part of the plot nearest the house. Pesticide I do not buy — only if fall armyworm comes badly I might try ash or a small sachet from the agro-dealer, but I do not plan for it.
